Subject: Post-call: Long-context evals & next steps (Acme)

Hi John / Sara -

Thanks again for the productive call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have alignment: 

Call recap:
- Scope: Acme is evaluating long-context summarization for multi-hour call transcripts and merged customer support threads (~50k-200k token documents).
- Key concerns: truncation behavior, summarization fidelity (abstractive vs extractive quality), and potential quality regressions after quantization/optimizations.
- Success criteria: (1) concise executive summaries that retain action items, (2) <10% drop vs human baseline on extractive recall metrics, (3) production latency targets <1.2s per 1k tokens for hosted pilots.

Recommended next steps (what we can do from Redwood):
1) Baseline eval: we'll run our long-context benchmark on a 100-sample corpus you provide (we suggest the 100 most representative transcripts). Please attach as NDJSON/JSONL with one document per line.
2) Model candidates: we recommend trying two variants in parallel: 
   - Mistral-Long-7B (open long-context variant) - low cost, good summary quality for <64k tokens.
   - Redwood-long-13B-compat (Redwood-verified long-context variant, quantized q4/q8) - better coherence on >64k tokens and stronger extractive fidelity.
3) Prompt sets & evals: we attached our suggested prompt set (acme-long-context-prompt-set-v1.jsonl) and a short eval rubric.
4) Pilot & timeline: run a 100-doc pilot (1-2 weeks) -> review metrics -> expand to 1k docs if results good.

Attachments included: acme-long-context-eval-report.pdf (initial template), acme-long-context-prompt-set-v1.jsonl, acme-sample-docs-100.jsonl (sample format).

Ask for you: could you share the sample 100 transcripts and confirm preferred pilot start week? Also flag any compliance/legal constraints we should be aware of (PII handling, retention windows).

I've CC'd Neha (quality/evals) and Dylan (runtime/latency) to help scope the pilot.

Thanks,

Hi John - great questions. Short answers up front, then details below.

TL;DR:
- Truncation/strategy: Redwood-long variants use an adaptive KV caching strategy + chunked two-stage summarization for very long docs (>64k). That means we keep a semantic index for earlier sections and prioritize recent sections for context in generation; for final executive summaries we run a second-pass global aggregator to reduce hallucination and increase extractive fidelity.
- Failure modes: repeated referential context ("see above"), highly nested timelines, and inconsistent speaker labels are the most common causes of missed items.
- Pricing: pilot 100-doc baseline on hosted API: ~USD 1.5k-2.5k depending on tuning/verbosity. 1k-doc run: ~USD 12k-18k. Dedicated pricing varies - happy to set up a quote if you want predictable throughput and an SLA.

More detail:
1) Behavior & truncation:
   - Up to 64k tokens: single-pass long attention / optimized kernels. Minimal truncation.
   - 64k-256k: we apply chunking + KV cache + two-pass aggregator. The first pass generates per-chunk summaries and a lightweight semantic index (embeddings). The second pass synthesizes a single executive summary from the chunk summaries using the index to recover long-range facts.
   - This approach reduces tail-truncation-induced hallucinations but you may still see omissions of very sparsely referenced facts; our evals measure that via extractive recall.

2) Summarization fidelity & regressions:
   - For fidelity we report both extractive recall (how many ground-truth items appear) and ROUGE-L / BLEU-style metrics for surface overlap. We also run an "action-item recall" metric focused on named entities and TODOs.
   - Quality regressions can occur after aggressive quantization (q4->q4_0) or when kernel fallback engages on atypical sequence lengths. We recommend running a control set (10% of corpus) across the quantized variants to detect regressions early.

3) Recommended models for your pilot (what to run in parallel):
   - Redwood-long-13B-compat (q8): Best coherence for >64k, higher cost but stronger extractive recall.
   - Mistral-Long-7B (fp16/opt): Lower cost, good for initial pass and faster throughput.
   - Fallback: Llama2-Chat-70k variant (if you need conversational tuning / speaker-aware prompts).

4) Metrics & evals we'll produce for each run:
   - Extractive recall (%), ROUGE-L, action-item F1, latency per 1k tokens, token cost per doc.

Next steps I suggest now:
- If you can, send the 100 documents (JSONL) and a short gold-reference set for 20 of them (human summaries) - that will let us compute extractive recall against a ground truth.
- We'll run the three variants and return a one-page summary + scorecard and a short sample comparison (side-by-side summaries).

Neha and Dev - looping you both to confirm the eval metrics and the compliance checklist John mentioned (PII retention). Neha: can you confirm the eval rubric we should use? Dev: quick note on any retention/ingestion limits we should flag for Acme.

Thanks,
Marissa

Marissa / team - quick internal note on evaluation setup before we hand this to Acme: 

- Eval rubric: I propose we compute (1) Extractive recall at top-K facts, (2) Action-item recall (entity + verb), (3) ROUGE-L for surface similarity, (4) Hallucination rate measured by a lightweight NER-backed validator against the doc store.
- Control/comparison: include a control set of 30 docs run on the current production model (baseline) + the three candidate variants. That will surface regressions introduced by quantization or kernel fallbacks.
- Prompt set: I reviewed the attached prompt set; suggest adding one conservative prompt that forces extractive-first behavior ("List all action items and their timestamps. If unsure, say 'uncertain' rather than guessing"). I'll add that to acme-long-context-prompt-set-v1.jsonl and return a v2.
- Data handling: Dev, confirm retention policy we should present to Acme for pilot: hosted -> default 30d logs + option for 90d with enterprise retention. Also confirm any PII redaction options pre-ingest.

I'll update the prompt set and return v2 by EOD. Marissa — once John shares samples I can precompute the eval harness to shorten turnaround.

Thanks,
